experiment: X10 discover-all: can we segment 'everything' without categories?

policy.scale: estimated (floor plane + assumed 1.6 m camera height) wherever metres appear (geometry lane only)
policy.agent_labelled: the reference letters and the own-look boxes are agent-labelled (Claude looking at images): reference.json, own-look.json, audit-sheets/*.jpg (letter stamped bottom right of each tile), own-look/*.jpg
policy.observed_vs_inferred: observed: every recall, precision, per-frame and stack time below; inferred: lines marked 'inferred'

setup.keyframe_rule: the core's: 5 fps = sharpest of each 6-frame block, object keyframes = every 3rd; 12 reference keyframes spread evenly over the object keyframes; 5 fps neighbours = the 5 fps keyframe before and after
setup.evaluation_grid: half resolution (640 x 360) for the 1280 x 720 clips, native 640 x 480 for lightning; every method's masks resized there (area > 0.3)

methods_as_used.SAM 3 word methods: the core's dedupe rule (segment.dedupe: IoU > 0.8 across words, >= 0.5 inside within a word)
methods_as_used.all: people out (>= 0.5 inside a SAM 3 person mask), masks < 24 px or > 0.6 of the frame dropped

licences.SAM 3: SAM License (Meta, custom; commercial use allowed with conditions)
licences.YOLO-World: not used: GPL-3.0 code, AGPL-3.0 via ultralytics
licences.Grounding DINO: not used (Apache-2.0); OWLv2 covered the box route

ram_plus.note: per frame = decode + 5 crops (full + 2x2 tiles) + one batched forward

reference_pool.how: every method's masks (as used) on the 48 reference frames, clustered at IoU >= 0.6 (19,575 clusters); a seeded stratified sample audited on contact sheets (thin-shaped clusters at 30%, the rest at 12%): W whole thing, T thin whole thing, K block of repeated things, P part, B background, M mixture, X unclear; W/T/K = reference items, weight 1/p
reference_pool.matching: found = a method mask with IoU >= 0.5 with the item (thin items: 1 px dilation on both), on a stride-2 grid; recall weighted by 1/p
reference_pool.bias: the pool is made of the methods' own masks: it cannot contain what no method outlined (see own_look), and it favours methods with many masks; the four later methods (ridge2, labelw, labelw_t, generic_t) were not in the pool: their pool recall is a lower bound

own_look.rule: own look at every other reference frame (6 per video): small and thin things an EHS inspector could care about, boxed on a 5% grid (units 0-20); classes: cable (cables, cords, hoses, wires), tool (hand and power tools, vises, clamps), label (labels, signs, placards, stickers), floor (loose items or debris on the floor), small (other small items: bins, cans, bottles, boxes, parts, electrical boxes)
own_look.matching: found = a mask whose box centre is inside the look box and box IoU >= 0.3 (the look boxes are read off a 5% grid)
own_look.note: independent of every method's masks: the completeness check of the pool reference

precision_pool_audit._rule: share of each method's masks (weighted by the audit sample) whose cluster was labelled whole (W/T/K), part (P), background (B), group/mixture (M) or unclear (X)

time_per_frame_one_a100.note: median over the 36 frames per video (48 for AMG 16 / c1, listing and geometry); 'added' = minus what the core already runs on its keyframes (SAM 3 vision features, DA3 depth, the vocabulary words' detection)

stack_added_s_two_a100.note: t0 = the core's state ready (keyframes on their GPU, SAM 3 features, person/floor): wall seconds until both GPUs finish; 2 threads, frames alternate; no MPS

five_fps_neighbours.rule: a reference item counts as found when found on its keyframe or on the 5 fps keyframe before / after, those masks warped onto the keyframe by DIS optical flow (lower bound: warping blurs thin masks)

summary.answer: No: SAM 2.1 automatic masks do not cut out 'everything'. On 48 keyframes of 4 videos, against an audited reference, AMG 16x16 found 11% of the things (own look 27%), 32x32 25% (47%), 32x32 with one crop layer 38% (60%) at 3.7 s a frame; thin things 3-16%; only 12-16% of its masks are one whole thing (50-59% parts, 19-21% background). What works is a union: the core's vocabulary + SAM 3 catch-all words + OWLv2 objectness boxes into SAM 2.1 + a label word set + ridge points for cables.

add_to_core: SAM 3 catch-all words on the kept features (generic: object, item, tool, cable, hose, debris, container, equipment, sign)
SAM 3 label words on the kept features (label, sticker, tag, sign, placard, price tag, warning label)
OWLv2-L objectness: top 100 boxes -> SAM 2.1-L box prompts (one image embedding per keyframe)
ridge2: Hessian ridges, straight ones dropped, 5 points along each -> SAM 2.1 multimask, the thinnest good mask (same embedding)
recommended_stack.added_s: 15.0-19.8 s measured on the object keyframes (42-50 per 30 s video), 2 A100-80GB, models resident; per-GPU peak 19.3 / 40.5 GB of 80 (every stack run: 22.58 / 43.78 GB; nothing over 90%)
recommended_stack.optional_small_items: the same two SAM 3 word sets on 2x2 tiles (labelw_t + generic_t) lift tiny things 0.57 -> 0.70 on the pool reference, but own look only 0.85 -> 0.86 and ~0.9 s a frame: inferred ~35-45 s, over the budget

not_recommended.SAM 2.1 AMG: amg16 adds 1 own-look item for +9-10 s; amg32 +3-5 points for +28-30 s; one crop layer 3.7 s a frame
not_recommended.RAM++ tags -> SAM 3: 0.30 / 0.39 alone, +2 points on the vocabulary, 0.46 s a frame; tags are scene words (pillar, shirt, subway)
not_recommended.OWLv2 words -> SAM 3: +4 points on the vocabulary for 0.33 s a frame; OWLv2's boxes carry the gain, not its words
not_recommended.3D geometry (planes + residual clusters): 6-9% alone; residuals are mostly parts and noise at DA3's 504x280 grid; cables on the floor are within the depth noise
not_recommended.Qwen3-VL-8B tiled listing: 0.43 / 0.53 at 16 s a frame: a reference tool, not a stage
not_recommended.5 fps object keyframes: thin items +0 to +3 of 75 per method (flow-warped lower bound), all items +3.6 to +5.6 points; the recommended stack at 5 fps is 42-54 s

what_still_gets_missed: small labels and price tags on beams and hooks (own look: 23 of 77 labels missed by the stack, 21 by every method)
pallets under a loaded stack (outlined together with the load)
tiny far things: fire-alarm strobes, e-stop buttons, a shoe on the floor far away (< 0.1% of the frame)
thin low-contrast or occluded cables: white cables under a bench, a red hose against a red machine, conduit on a white wall
floor tape lines and barrier tape (outlined as floor)
a box leaning out of a shelf, open boxes (merged into the shelf contents)
things a person partly hides (people masks are cut out first)

table_stacks.added_s_video_2_a100: 24.3-30.2 s measured (with ridge2 in place of ridge)
inferred ~35-45 s: 15-20 s measured stack + (0.43 + 0.47 s per frame x 42-50 keyframes / 2 GPUs)
inferred ~80-95 s: 3.7 s per frame x 42-50 keyframes / 2 GPUs
minutes (inferred; the Qwen listing alone 16 s per frame)

caveats: pool reference = union of the methods' own masks, audited on a stratified sample (2,835 of 19,575 clusters): recall is relative to what some method outlined; the own look (342 boxes on 25 frames) is the independent check, box-matched leniently
agent-labelled throughout (Claude), not a human; retail shelves were labelled at block level (K), single products as parts
stack times start from the core's state (features, person/floor, depth) and exclude the vocabulary itself; no MPS in these runs
the summary text was written by hand from the numbers in this file
